prompt:
Scene:
A square-format photograph of the same municipal indoor pool mid-maintenance: the basin has been fully drained and scraped back to raw concrete. Scaffolding props lean against the near wall, a coiled orange extension cord snakes across the deck, a single worklamp on a tripod points into the basin. Ceiling fluorescents are partially on, giving a flat sickly green ambient. The photographer fires a direct flash. 35mm grain, yellowish cast typical of over-exposed consumer film.

Subject:
Same pool footprint and lane count as the reference, same camera vantage. But here the wall tiles have been partly removed, showing exposed cementitious backer and rust streaks on rebar hints. The lane painted stripes at the bottom are scuffed and faded. The metal ladder is unbolted and lying on the deck. A polyethylene construction sheet hangs along one wall. The air reads as concrete dust, not chlorine.

Important details:
Preserve the basin's overall shape, lane count, and camera viewpoint from the reference. Only the finish material and activity state differ: finishes stripped, maintenance gear introduced, ladder displaced. No worker present in frame. The uncanny beat: midway between 'functional pool' and 'forgotten pool'. Flash hotspot should land on the scraped wall, revealing material layers. No lens flare, no cinematic grade.

Use case:
Series image 4 of 4. Preserves reference basin in stripped maintenance state.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no worker or person, no power tools in active use, no photographer reflection on plastic sheet, no warped tile geometry.
title: Pool · Stripped Maintenance
description: Same reference pool mid-renovation, tiles partially removed and scaffolding introduced, preserving basin footprint and vantage.
